claims.text: Nanoparticles containing five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios can maintain structural and chemical stability during operation from 473 to 1923 K.
A stable solid-solution phase governs the maintenance of structural and chemical stability over this temperature range.
The stable solid-solution phase resists phase separation.
The initial nanoparticles are solid solutions composed of at least five metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
The nanoparticles are subjected to thermal cycling between 473 and 1923 K.
Maintaining a constant controlled atmosphere prevents oxidation or contamination during thermal cycling.
A solid-solution phase provides a uniform distribution of the constituent metals.
Uniform metal distribution prevents segregation during thermal stress.
Preventing segregation maintains nanoparticle structural integrity under thermal stress.
After thermal cycling, the nanoparticles will show minimal structural changes relative to their initial state.
After thermal cycling, the nanoparticles will show minimal chemical changes relative to their initial state.
The proposed behavior is limited to initially solid-solution nanoparticles containing at least five metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
